A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

dietary corn oil, at constant caloric intake, has a biphasic effect on skin tumor development in SENCAR mouse: (a) feeding high corn oil diet following DMBA treatment inhibits initiation, but (b) feeding high corn fat diet following initiation and during TPA treatment enhances promotion of the initiated tumors.

dietary fat influences the initiation phase of skin tumorigenies by reducing the multiplicity of papillomas, whereas dietary fat increases tumor multiplicity and the incidence of carcinomas when fed during the promotion phase of skin tumor development in SENCAR mouse.
dietary corn oil has no effect on the initiation of skin tumor formation, but it increases the number of papilomas formed per effective mouse, which is indicative of a promotion effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that

dietary fat can influence the development of skin cancer in mice, but that this influence is dependent on the timing of dietary fat consumption relative to the initiation and promotion stages of skin tumorigenis.
